thread.title: Apple Hammers Google and Amazon Over Privacy

author: Barron's
title: Apple Hammers Google and Amazon Over Privacy
text:
Photograph by Robyn Beck / AFP/Getty Images LAS VEGAS- Apple isn't at the Consumer Electronics Show this week, but it's making a big impression with an eye-catching billboard that goes after the privacy inadequacies of its major rivals.
The multi-story message on the side of a building abutting the Las Vegas Convention Center , or LVCC-"What happens on your iPhone stays on your iPhone."-is a not-too-subtle dig at Facebook (ticker: FB), Amazon.com ( AMZN ) and Alphabet's ( GOOGL ) Google. Both Amazon and Google have released news about their voice assistants at the sprawling conference.
The stark, black-and-white board towers above Google's booth at the conference. A link at the bottom, apple.com/privacy , explains the security of services such as Apple Pay and Face ID, as well as health data collected by Apple Watch.
https://asset.barrons.com/dj-mg/dice/barrons-staffpicks-2d590600-c862-4394-b9d3-66b48c376d60/inset.json
Privacy could be Apple's best bet to gain traction at a show it doesn't officially take part in, but where hundreds of device makers and software developers support the Apple computing platform. The topic is a favorite talking point of Apple ( AAPL ) Chief Executive Tim Cook, who argues that his company's largely ad-free business model puts privacy above the monetization of data. That, he says, differentiates the company from businesses such as Google and Facebook.
Amazon and Google didn't immediately respond to requests for comment. Facebook declined to comment.
Amazon's Alexa has had some serious miscues, such as mistakenly sending one person 1,700 voice recordings from a stranger. Google Assistant has had some slipups of its own, including Android device makers surreptitiously tracking user information .
After one of the roughest patches in its history, in which its stock was pummeled after Cook warned of softening sales in China, Apple needs a new conversation.
Google hopes to create plenty of buzz of its own. It has constructed a massive facility outside the convention center, and says it will use it to announce "major news" for Google Assistant on Tuesday. The Silicon Valley company has plastered the LVCC and Las Vegas' monorail with Google banners.
Write to Jon Swartz at jonathan.swartz@dowjones.com
